records.query: Need the patient's skin biopsy pathology report with immunohistochemistry (core basis for confirming cutaneous lymphoma and excluding inflammatory dermatoses).

Need the patient's T-cell receptor gene rearrangement and flow cytometry results from the skin biopsy specimen (core for confirming clonal T-cell population and distinguishing cutaneous lymphoma from reactive inflammatory infiltrates).

Need the skin biopsy histopathology and immunohistochemistry report from the right axillary lesion, including T-cell receptor gene rearrangement analysis, as these are core tests to confirm or exclude cutaneous lymphoma.

Need the complete blood count with differential, peripheral blood smear review, and serum lactate dehydrogenase level to assess for systemic involvement and support the diagnosis of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma, as these are key ancillary tests.

Need the patient's complete blood count, peripheral blood smear, and serum lactate dehydrogenase results, as these systemic workup findings are essential for assessing extracutaneous involvement and supporting the diagnosis of cutaneous lymphoma.

Need the patient's whole-body PET-CT or CT imaging staging results, as these are essential for evaluating extracutaneous lymphoma involvement and determining disease stage, which directly impacts prognosis and treatment planning for suspected cutaneous T-cell lymphoma.

Need flow cytometry immunophenotyping of the skin biopsy and peripheral blood to detect aberrant T-cell populations and confirm clonality, as this is the remaining core test to support mycosis fungoides and distinguish it from reactive inflammatory dermatoses.

Need the patient's staging imaging (CT chest/abdomen/pelvis or PET-CT) and lymph node ultrasound, plus serum calcium, uric acid, and liver function tests, to assess for systemic involvement and stage the suspected cutaneous lymphoma; these are critical missing data that determine whether the disease is skin-limited or advanced and guide confirmatory biopsy interpretation.

Need the patient's peripheral blood flow cytometry and TCR gene rearrangement results, including CD4/CD8 ratio, CD4+CD7- and CD4+CD26- T-cell counts, to assess for Sézary syndrome and extracutaneous leukemic involvement, which is essential for staging and confirming mycosis fungoides.

Need the patient's complete dermatological examination record detailing lesion distribution, number, size, morphology (patch/plaque), duration and progression, along with palpable lymph node and organomegaly assessment, as these clinical findings are essential for refining the suspicion of patch-stage mycosis fungoides and guiding biopsy site selection and staging.

These findings are critical to clinically stage suspected mycosis fungoides, distinguish patch-stage from more advanced disease, and guide interpretation of the pending biopsy and imaging results.

Need the finalized dermatopathology report detailing epidermotropism, Pautrier microabscesses, and T-cell marker profile (CD2, CD3, CD4, CD5, CD7, CD8), together with TCR gene rearrangement and PET-CT staging results, as these are the decisive missing data to confirm or exclude patch-stage mycosis fungoides and rule out systemic involvement.

bindings.label: A man in his 40s presented with a 3-month history of discrete, dark red, circular lesions in his right axilla
The patient reported severe pruritus at these sites that would wake him up at night

Physical examination revealed 3 well-circumscribed, violaceous, annular patches without scale or erosion limited to the right axilla; no other lesions were noted on skin or mucous membranes; Wood lamp examination was negative
The patient denied recent trauma, history of similar lesions, associated pain, blisters, or systemic symptoms; medical history was unremarkable; no environmental triggers or new medications
Treatment with over-the-counter hydrocortisone cream, ketoconazole cream, and discontinuation of underarm deodorant yielded no improvement
Skin biopsy with histopathology, immunohistochemistry, TCR gene rearrangement, and flow cytometry has been requested but results are pending
CBC with differential, peripheral smear, and serum LDH have been ordered to assess systemic involvement but results are not yet available
The right axillary lesion is mycosis fungoides (cutaneous T-cell lymphoma)
Staging imaging (e.g., CT/PET) has been recommended but results are not yet available
Primary cutaneous CD30+ lymphoproliferative disorder (e.g., primary cutaneous anaplastic large cell lymphoma)
Other cutaneous T-cell lymphoma (e.g., Sézary syndrome, peripheral T-cell lymphoma)
H&E of skin biopsy shows epidermotropism
Peripheral blood flow cytometry has been requested but results are not yet available
